text: No code word may be a prefix of another, so a decoder reading left to right knows a symbol has ended without lookahead or separators. Such a code is called a ___ code.
explanation: It is equivalent to putting the symbols at the leaves of a binary tree, since no leaf is an ancestor of another — which is why Huffman's algorithm builds one. UTF-8 is a prefix code, which is why a decoder that lands mid-character can resynchronise by scanning forward for a byte that does not begin with 10.
